#' Multi-Metric Healthiness Assessment for UK Foods and Out-of-Home Menus
#'
#' Evaluates food and drink products across candidate UK healthiness assessment
#' approaches:
#' \enumerate{
#'   \item \strong{UK Nutrient Profile Model (NPM)}: Statutory 2004/2005 (DHSC 2011) or 2018 model.
#'   \item \strong{Multiple Traffic Light Labelling (MTL)}: Front-of-pack green/amber/red criteria per 100g and per portion.
#'   \item \strong{UK Reduction Programmes and Levy}: Soft Drinks Industry Levy (SDIL), OHID 2024 salt reduction targets, sugar reduction targets, and calorie guidelines.
#'   \item \strong{Combined Approaches}: Hybrid NPM + MTL portion caps, reflecting recommendations from Tan et al. (2025) for out-of-home (OOH) food.
#' }
#'
#' @param data A \code{data.frame} containing product nutritional information. If \code{NULL},
#'   individual column vectors may be supplied.
#' @param energy_kj Numeric vector or column name for energy in kJ per 100g.
#' @param energy_kcal Numeric vector or column name for energy in kcal per 100g.
#' @param energy_kcal_portion Numeric vector or column name for energy in kcal per portion.
#' @param fat_g Numeric vector or column name for total fat in g per 100g.
#' @param sat_fat_g Numeric vector or column name for saturated fat in g per 100g.
#' @param sugars_g Numeric vector or column name for total sugars in g per 100g.
#' @param free_sugars_g Optional numeric vector or column name for free sugars in g per 100g.
#' @param salt_g Numeric vector or column name for salt in g per 100g.
#' @param sodium_mg Optional numeric vector or column name for sodium in mg per 100g.
#' @param fvns_pct Numeric vector or column name for fruit, veg, nuts (and seeds) percentage.
#' @param fibre_g Numeric vector or column name for fibre in g per 100g.
#' @param protein_g Numeric vector or column name for protein in g per 100g.
#' @param portion_g Optional numeric vector or column name for portion weight in g (or ml).
#' @param category Optional character vector or column name specifying food category.
#' @param is_drink Logical vector or column name indicating whether item is a drink (\code{TRUE}) or food (\code{FALSE}).
#' @param is_cheese Logical vector indicating whether item is cheese.
#' @param npm_model Character string for NPM version: \code{"2004_2005"} or \code{"2018"}.
#'
#' @return A \code{data.frame} augmented with all assessment metrics:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{npm_score}{NPM score.}
#'   \item{npm_is_hfss}{NPM HFSS flag (\code{TRUE} = less healthy).}
#'   \item{npm_healthiness}{\code{"healthier"} vs \code{"less healthy"}.}
#'   \item{mtl_fat}{Colour code for fat.}
#'   \item{mtl_sat_fat}{Colour code for saturated fat.}
#'   \item{mtl_sugars}{Colour code for sugars.}
#'   \item{mtl_salt}{Colour code for salt.}
#'   \item{mtl_n_red}{Count of Red traffic lights (0--4).}
#'   \item{mtl_has_red}{Logical indicating \eqn{\ge 1} Red lights.}
#'   \item{mtl_healthiness}{\code{"healthier"} (0 red) vs \code{"less healthy"} (\eqn{\ge 1} red).}
#'   \item{sdil_tier}{Levy tier for drinks.}
#'   \item{meets_salt_target}{Compliance with OHID salt targets (if category matched).}
#'   \item{meets_sugar_target}{Compliance with OHID sugar targets (if category matched).}
#'   \item{meets_calorie_guideline}{Compliance with calorie guidelines (if portion kcal provided).}
#'   \item{combined_npm_mtl_healthy}{Logical indicating healthy under both NPM and MTL (\code{!npm_is_hfss & !mtl_has_red}).}
#' }
#'
#' @references
#' Tan M, Pham H, Pombo-Rodrigues S, Hashem KM, Shiach A, Barakat NA (2025).
#' Nutritional composition and healthiness of out-of-home food and drink: cross-sectional
#' and retrospective longitudinal analyses of best-selling menu items in the UK, 2021-2023/24.
#' \emph{Proceedings of the Nutrition Society}, 84(OCE3), E208. \doi{10.1017/S0029665125100773}
#'
#' @examples
#' # Assess a sample meal (burger with 650 kcal, 25g fat, 8g sat fat, 5g sugar, 2.2g salt):
#' sample_burger <- data.frame(
#'   item = "Classic Cheeseburger",
#'   energy_kcal = 260,
#'   energy_kcal_portion = 650,
#'   fat_g = 12.0,
#'   sat_fat_g = 5.5,
#'   sugars_g = 3.5,
#'   salt_g = 1.3,
#'   fvns_pct = 5,
#'   fibre_g = 1.8,
#'   protein_g = 14.0,
#'   portion_g = 250,
#'   category = "Main meal",
#'   is_drink = FALSE
#' )
#' assess_healthiness(sample_burger)
#'
#' @export
assess_healthiness <- function(data = NULL,
                               energy_kj = NULL,
                               energy_kcal = NULL,
                               energy_kcal_portion = NULL,
                               fat_g = NULL,
                               sat_fat_g = NULL,
                               sugars_g = NULL,
                               free_sugars_g = NULL,
                               salt_g = NULL,
                               sodium_mg = NULL,
                               fvns_pct = NULL,
                               fibre_g = NULL,
                               protein_g = NULL,
                               portion_g = NULL,
                               category = NULL,
                               is_drink = FALSE,
                               is_cheese = FALSE,
                               npm_model = c("2004_2005", "2018")) {
  npm_model <- match.arg(npm_model)

  # Extract from data.frame if supplied
  resolve_col <- function(col_name, direct_val, df) {
    if (!is.null(direct_val)) return(direct_val)
    if (!is.null(df) && is.character(col_name) && length(col_name) == 1 && col_name %in% names(df)) {
      return(df[[col_name]])
    }
    NULL
  }

  e_kj <- resolve_col("energy_kj", energy_kj, data)
  e_kcal <- resolve_col("energy_kcal", energy_kcal, data)
  e_kcal_p <- resolve_col("energy_kcal_portion", energy_kcal_portion, data)
  fat <- resolve_col("fat_g", fat_g, data)
  sf <- resolve_col("sat_fat_g", sat_fat_g, data)
  sug <- resolve_col("sugars_g", sugars_g, data)
  fsug <- resolve_col("free_sugars_g", free_sugars_g, data)
  salt <- resolve_col("salt_g", salt_g, data)
  na <- resolve_col("sodium_mg", sodium_mg, data)
  fvns <- resolve_col("fvns_pct", fvns_pct, data)
  fib <- resolve_col("fibre_g", fibre_g, data)
  prot <- resolve_col("protein_g", protein_g, data)
  port <- resolve_col("portion_g", portion_g, data)
  cat_v <- resolve_col("category", category, data)
  drk <- resolve_col("is_drink", is_drink, data)
  chs <- resolve_col("is_cheese", is_cheese, data)

  if (is.null(fat)) fat <- 0
  if (is.null(sf)) sf <- 0
  if (is.null(sug)) sug <- 0
  if (is.null(fvns)) fvns <- 0
  if (is.null(fib)) fib <- 0
  if (is.null(prot)) prot <- 0
  if (is.null(drk)) drk <- FALSE
  if (is.null(chs)) chs <- FALSE

  # If energy_kcal_portion not provided but energy_kcal and portion_g are:
  if (is.null(e_kcal_p) && !is.null(e_kcal) && !is.null(port)) {
    e_kcal_p <- e_kcal * port / 100
  }

  # 1. NPM calculation
  npm_res <- calculate_npm(
    energy_kj = e_kj,
    energy_kcal = e_kcal,
    sat_fat_g = sf,
    sugars_g = sug,
    free_sugars_g = fsug,
    sodium_mg = na,
    salt_g = salt,
    fvns_pct = fvns,
    fibre_g = fib,
    protein_g = prot,
    is_drink = drk,
    is_cheese = chs,
    model = npm_model
  )

  # 2. MTL calculation
  mtl_res <- calculate_mtl(
    fat_g = fat,
    sat_fat_g = sf,
    sugars_g = sug,
    salt_g = salt,
    sodium_mg = na,
    portion_g = port,
    is_drink = drk
  )

  # 3. SDIL calculation (for drinks)
  sdil_res <- calculate_sdil(sugars_g_100ml = sug, is_exempt = !drk)

  # 4. Salt target check (if category provided)
  if (!is.null(cat_v)) {
    salt_chk <- check_salt_target(salt_g_100g = if (!is.null(salt)) salt else 0, category = cat_v)
    meets_salt <- salt_chk$salt_compliant
  } else {
    meets_salt <- rep(NA, nrow(npm_res))
  }

  # 5. Sugar target check (if category provided)
  if (!is.null(cat_v)) {
    sugar_chk <- check_sugar_target(sugars_g_100g = sug, category = cat_v)
    meets_sugar <- sugar_chk$sugar_compliant
  } else {
    meets_sugar <- rep(NA, nrow(npm_res))
  }

  # 6. Calorie guideline check (if portion kcal provided)
  if (!is.null(e_kcal_p)) {
    cal_chk <- check_calorie_guideline(energy_kcal_portion = e_kcal_p, category = cat_v)
    meets_cal <- cal_chk$meets_calorie_guideline
  } else {
    meets_cal <- rep(NA, nrow(npm_res))
  }

  # Combined metric (Tan et al. 2025): Healthy under both NPM and MTL portion flags
  combined_healthy <- (!npm_res$is_hfss) & (!mtl_res$has_red)

  out <- data.frame(
    npm_score = npm_res$npm_score,
    npm_is_hfss = npm_res$is_hfss,
    npm_healthiness = npm_res$healthiness,
    mtl_fat = mtl_res$fat_colour,
    mtl_sat_fat = mtl_res$sat_fat_colour,
    mtl_sugars = mtl_res$sugars_colour,
    mtl_salt = mtl_res$salt_colour,
    mtl_n_red = mtl_res$n_red,
    mtl_has_red = mtl_res$has_red,
    mtl_healthiness = mtl_res$mtl_healthiness,
    sdil_tier = ifelse(drk, sdil_res$sdil_tier, "Not applicable (Food)"),
    meets_salt_target = meets_salt,
    meets_sugar_target = meets_sugar,
    meets_calorie_guideline = meets_cal,
    combined_npm_mtl_healthy = combined_healthy,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  if (!is.null(data)) {
    return(cbind(data, out))
  }
  out
}

#' Summarise Healthiness Across Candidate Assessment Approaches
#'
#' Generates comparative summary statistics (% classified as healthy vs less healthy)
#' across all candidate assessment approaches evaluated by \code{\link{assess_healthiness}},
#' replicating the comparative reporting methodology of Tan et al. (2025).
#'
#' @param assessment_df A data frame returned by \code{\link{assess_healthiness}}.
#'
#' @return A \code{data.frame} summarizing each candidate approach:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{approach}{Candidate healthiness assessment framework.}
#'   \item{total_items}{Total evaluated items.}
#'   \item{n_healthy}{Count of items classified as healthy / compliant.}
#'   \item{pct_healthy}{Percentage of items classified as healthy.}
#'   \item{n_less_healthy}{Count of items classified as less healthy / non-compliant.}
#'   \item{pct_less_healthy}{Percentage of items classified as less healthy.}
#' }
#'
#' @references
#' Tan M, Pham H, Pombo-Rodrigues S, et al. (2025). Nutritional composition and healthiness of out-of-home food and drink.
#' \emph{Proceedings of the Nutrition Society}, 84(OCE3), E208.
#'
#' @export
summarise_healthiness <- function(assessment_df) {
  n_total <- nrow(assessment_df)

  # Approaches:
  # 1. NPM (Healthier = !npm_is_hfss)
  npm_healthy <- sum(!assessment_df$npm_is_hfss, na.rm = TRUE)

  # 2. MTL (Healthier = !mtl_has_red, i.e. 0 red lights)
  mtl_healthy <- sum(!assessment_df$mtl_has_red, na.rm = TRUE)

  # 3. Combined NPM + MTL
  comb_healthy <- sum(assessment_df$combined_npm_mtl_healthy, na.rm = TRUE)

  approaches <- c(
    "UK Nutrient Profile Model (NPM)",
    "Multiple Traffic Light (MTL, No Red Lights)",
    "Combined NPM + MTL Portion Caps"
  )
  healthy_counts <- c(npm_healthy, mtl_healthy, comb_healthy)

  # Add reduction programmes if present
  if (any(!is.na(assessment_df$meets_calorie_guideline))) {
    approaches <- c(approaches, "UK Calorie Reduction Guidelines")
    healthy_counts <- c(healthy_counts, sum(assessment_df$meets_calorie_guideline == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  if (any(!is.na(assessment_df$meets_salt_target))) {
    approaches <- c(approaches, "UK Salt Reduction 2024 Targets")
    healthy_counts <- c(healthy_counts, sum(assessment_df$meets_salt_target == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE))
  }
  if (any(!is.na(assessment_df$meets_sugar_target))) {
    approaches <- c(approaches, "UK Sugar Reduction Targets")
    healthy_counts <- c(healthy_counts, sum(assessment_df$meets_sugar_target == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE))
  }

  less_healthy_counts <- n_total - healthy_counts
  pct_h <- round((healthy_counts / n_total) * 100, 1)
  pct_lh <- round((less_healthy_counts / n_total) * 100, 1)

  data.frame(
    approach = approaches,
    total_items = rep(n_total, length(approaches)),
    n_healthy = healthy_counts,
    pct_healthy = pct_h,
    n_less_healthy = less_healthy_counts,
    pct_less_healthy = pct_lh,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

name: R/fvns.R
content:
#' Calculate Fruit, Vegetables, Nuts and Seeds (FVNS) Percentage
#'
#' Calculates the percentage of fruit, vegetables, nuts, and seeds (FVNS) in a
#' food or drink product according to the UK Department of Health and Social Care
#' (DHSC) Nutrient Profiling Technical Guidance (2011) and NPM 2018 guidance.
#'
#' Under the official guidance, dried fruits and vegetables are concentrated
#' and therefore their weight is multiplied by 2 when calculating the proportion
#' of FVNS in composite foods:
#' \deqn{\% \text{FVNS} = \frac{W_{\text{fresh}} + (2 \times W_{\text{dried}})}{W_{\text{fresh}} + (2 \times W_{\text{dried}}) + W_{\text{other}}} \times 100}
#'
#' Minimally processed fruit and vegetables (including fresh, frozen, cooked, canned,
#' 100\% pure juices, and purees) count towards FVNS. Concentrated fruit juice
#' sugars, powders, or leathers do not count. Potatoes and other starchy tubers
#' (such as yams and cassava) do not count.
#'
#' @param weight_fvns Numeric vector of weights (in grams) of intact, fresh,
#'   cooked, canned, or pureed fruit, vegetables, nuts (and seeds in 2018 model).
#'   Default is 0.
#' @param weight_dried Numeric vector of weights (in grams) of dried fruit, dried
#'   vegetables, or concentrated tomato puree (which receives the 2x multiplier).
#'   Default is 0.
#' @param weight_other Numeric vector of weights (in grams) of other ingredients
#'   in the product (e.g. cereals, flour, sugar, fat, water, meat, dairy).
#' @param total_weight Optional numeric vector of total product weight. If provided
#'   and `weight_other` is `NULL`, `weight_other` is inferred as
#'   `total_weight - weight_fvns - weight_dried`.
#'
#' @return A numeric vector representing the percentage (0 to 100) of FVNS in the product.
#' @references
#' Department of Health and Social Care (2011). \emph{Nutrient Profiling Technical Guidance}.
#' Department of Health and Social Care (2018). \emph{Nutrient Profiling Model 2018: Technical Guidance}.
#'
#' @examples
#' # Worked Example 5 from DHSC 2011 Guidance:
#' # Fruit and nut cereal bar containing 30g dried fruit per 100g (70g other ingredients):
#' calculate_fvns(weight_fvns = 0, weight_dried = 30, weight_other = 70)
#' # Expected output: 46.15% (rounds to 46% as in guidance)
#'
#' # Pure 100% fruit juice:
#' calculate_fvns(weight_fvns = 100, weight_other = 0)
#'
#' @export
calculate_fvns <- function(weight_fvns = 0,
                           weight_dried = 0,
                           weight_other = NULL,
                           total_weight = NULL) {
  # Normalize inputs to numeric vectors
  n <- max(length(weight_fvns), length(weight_dried),
           if (!is.null(weight_other)) length(weight_other) else 0,
           if (!is.null(total_weight)) length(total_weight) else 0)

  weight_fvns <- rep_len(as.numeric(weight_fvns), n)
  weight_dried <- rep_len(as.numeric(weight_dried), n)

  weight_fvns[is.na(weight_fvns)] <- 0
  weight_dried[is.na(weight_dried)] <- 0

  if (is.null(weight_other)) {
    if (is.null(total_weight)) {
      stop("Either `weight_other` or `total_weight` must be specified.")
    }
    total_weight <- rep_len(as.numeric(total_weight), n)
    weight_other <- total_weight - weight_fvns - weight_dried
    weight_other <- pmax(weight_other, 0)
  } else {
    weight_other <- rep_len(as.numeric(weight_other), n)
    weight_other[is.na(weight_other)] <- 0
  }

  numerator <- weight_fvns + (2 * weight_dried)
  denominator <- numerator + weight_other

  pct <- ifelse(denominator <= 0, 0, (numerator / denominator) * 100)
  pmin(pmax(pct, 0), 100)
}

#' Calculate UK Nutrient Profile Model (NPM) Score and HFSS Classification
#'
#' Computes the nutrient profile score and High in Fat, Salt, or Sugar (HFSS)
#' classification under the official UK Nutrient Profile Model. Supports both
#' the statutory 2004/2005 model (DHSC 2011 Technical Guidance) used in Ofcom
#' broadcast restrictions and HFSS promotional/placement regulations, as well as
#' the updated NPM 2018 consultation model (DHSC 2018).
#'
#' Under the UK NPM, foods and drinks are scored based on nutrient content per 100g
#' (or 100ml converted by specific gravity). Points are allocated for "A" nutrients
#' to limit (energy, saturated fat, sugars, sodium/salt) and "C" components to
#' encourage (fruit, vegetables, nuts, seeds, fibre, protein).
#'
#' \strong{Protein Cap Rule:} If a food or drink scores 11 or more 'A' points,
#' it cannot score points for protein unless it also achieves 5 points for fruit,
#' vegetables, and nuts (or seeds in 2018). If the product is cheese, an exception
#' can be granted by setting \code{is_cheese = TRUE}, allowing protein points to
#' be retained.
#'
#' \strong{Classification Thresholds:}
#' \itemize{
#'   \item \strong{Food}: Score \eqn{\ge 4} is classified as \code{"less healthy"} (HFSS); score \eqn{< 4} is \code{"healthier"}.
#'   \item \strong{Drink}: Score \eqn{\ge 1} is classified as \code{"less healthy"} (HFSS); score \eqn{< 1} is \code{"healthier"}.
#' }
#'
#' @param energy_kj Numeric vector of energy in kilojoules (kJ) per 100g. If \code{NULL},
#'   can be derived from \code{energy_kcal} (\eqn{1\text{ kcal} = 4.184\text{ kJ}}).
#' @param energy_kcal Numeric vector of energy in kilocalories (kcal) per 100g. Used
#'   if \code{energy_kj} is not provided.
#' @param sat_fat_g Numeric vector of saturated fatty acids in grams (g) per 100g.
#' @param sugars_g Numeric vector of total sugars (in 2004/2005 model) or free sugars
#'   (in 2018 model) in grams (g) per 100g.
#' @param free_sugars_g Numeric vector of free sugars in grams (g) per 100g. Specifically
#'   utilised in the 2018 model. If \code{NULL} and \code{model = "2018"}, \code{sugars_g}
#'   is used.
#' @param sodium_mg Numeric vector of sodium in milligrams (mg) per 100g. If \code{NULL},
#'   calculated from \code{salt_g} (\eqn{\text{sodium (mg)} = \text{salt (g)} \times 1000 / 2.5}).
#' @param salt_g Numeric vector of salt (sodium chloride equivalent) in grams (g) per 100g.
#' @param fvns_pct Numeric vector of percentage of fruit, vegetables, nuts (and seeds in
#'   2018 model), between 0 and 100.
#' @param fibre_g Numeric vector of dietary fibre in grams (g) per 100g.
#' @param fibre_method Character string specifying the fibre measurement method:
#'   \code{"aoac"} (Association of Official Analytical Chemists) or \code{"nsp"}
#'   (Englyst Non-Starch Polysaccharide). Default is \code{"aoac"}. In the 2018 model,
#'   AOAC fibre is standard.
#' @param protein_g Numeric vector of protein in grams (g) per 100g.
#' @param is_drink Logical vector indicating whether the product is a beverage/drink
#'   (\code{TRUE}) or a food (\code{FALSE}). Default is \code{FALSE}.
#' @param is_cheese Logical vector indicating whether the product is cheese. If \code{TRUE},
#'   protein points are credited even if \eqn{\text{Total A} \ge 11}. Default is \code{FALSE}.
#' @param model Character string specifying the NPM version: \code{"2004_2005"}
#'   (statutory DHSC 2011 guidance) or \code{"2018"} (DHSC 2018 consultation model).
#'   Default is \code{"2004_2005"}.
#'
#' @return A \code{data.frame} containing:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{points_energy}{Points awarded for energy (0--10).}
#'   \item{points_sat_fat}{Points awarded for saturated fat (0--10).}
#'   \item{points_sugars}{Points awarded for sugars (0--10).}
#'   \item{points_sodium_salt}{Points awarded for sodium or salt (0--10).}
#'   \item{points_a}{Total 'A' points (0--40).}
#'   \item{points_fvns}{Points awarded for fruit, vegetables, nuts, seeds (0, 1, 2, or 5).}
#'   \item{points_fibre}{Points awarded for fibre (0--5 for 2004/2005; 0--10 for 2018).}
#'   \item{points_protein_raw}{Potential points from protein before capping (0--5).}
#'   \item{protein_allowed}{Logical indicating whether protein points are permitted.}
#'   \item{points_protein}{Actual points awarded for protein (0--5).}
#'   \item{points_c}{Total 'C' points.}
#'   \item{npm_score}{Final nutrient profile score (\code{points_a - points_c}).}
#'   \item{is_hfss}{Logical indicating if product is High in Fat, Salt, or Sugar (\code{TRUE} / \code{FALSE}).}
#'   \item{healthiness}{Character string: \code{"less healthy"} or \code{"healthier"}.}
#'   \item{model}{Model version applied.}
#' }
#'
#' @references
#' Department of Health and Social Care (2011). \emph{Nutrient Profiling Technical Guidance}.
#' \url{https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-nutrient-profiling-model}
#'
#' Department of Health and Social Care (2018). \emph{Nutrient Profiling Model 2018: Technical Guidance}.
#' \url{https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/nutrient-profiling-model-2018}
#'
#' @examples
#' # DHSC 2011 Worked Example 1: Fruit fromage frais per 100g
#' calculate_npm(
#'   energy_kj = 459,
#'   sat_fat_g = 1.8,
#'   sugars_g = 13.4,
#'   salt_g = 0.05,
#'   fvns_pct = 8,
#'   fibre_g = 0.6,
#'   protein_g = 6.5,
#'   is_drink = FALSE
#' )
#'
#' # DHSC 2011 Worked Example 2: Vanilla ice cream per 100g
#' calculate_npm(
#'   energy_kj = 741,
#'   sat_fat_g = 6.1,
#'   sugars_g = 18.7,
#'   sodium_mg = 60,
#'   fvns_pct = 0,
#'   fibre_g = 0,
#'   protein_g = 3.6,
#'   is_drink = FALSE
#' )
#'
#' @export
calculate_npm <- function(energy_kj = NULL,
                          energy_kcal = NULL,
                          sat_fat_g = 0,
                          sugars_g = 0,
                          free_sugars_g = NULL,
                          sodium_mg = NULL,
                          salt_g = NULL,
                          fvns_pct = 0,
                          fibre_g = 0,
                          fibre_method = c("aoac", "nsp"),
                          protein_g = 0,
                          is_drink = FALSE,
                          is_cheese = FALSE,
                          model = c("2004_2005", "2018"),
                          version = NULL) {
  fibre_method <- match.arg(fibre_method)
  if (!is.null(version)) {
    if (version %in% c("2004", "2004_2005")) {
      model <- "2004_2005"
    } else if (version %in% c("2018")) {
      model <- "2018"
    }
  }
  model <- match.arg(model)

  # Derive maximum vector length across all inputs
  lens <- c(
    if (!is.null(energy_kj)) length(energy_kj) else 0,
    if (!is.null(energy_kcal)) length(energy_kcal) else 0,
    length(sat_fat_g),
    length(sugars_g),
    if (!is.null(free_sugars_g)) length(free_sugars_g) else 0,
    if (!is.null(sodium_mg)) length(sodium_mg) else 0,
    if (!is.null(salt_g)) length(salt_g) else 0,
    length(fvns_pct),
    length(fibre_g),
    length(protein_g),
    length(is_drink),
    length(is_cheese)
  )
  n <- max(lens, 1)

  # Process energy (kJ vs kcal)
  if (is.null(energy_kj)) {
    if (is.null(energy_kcal)) {
      energy_kj <- rep_len(0, n)
    } else {
      energy_kcal <- rep_len(as.numeric(energy_kcal), n)
      energy_kj <- energy_kcal * 4.184
    }
  } else {
    energy_kj <- rep_len(as.numeric(energy_kj), n)
  }
  energy_kj[is.na(energy_kj)] <- 0

  # Saturated fat
  sat_fat_g <- rep_len(as.numeric(sat_fat_g), n)
  sat_fat_g[is.na(sat_fat_g)] <- 0

  # Sugars
  sugars_g <- rep_len(as.numeric(sugars_g), n)
  sugars_g[is.na(sugars_g)] <- 0

  if (!is.null(free_sugars_g)) {
    free_sugars_g <- rep_len(as.numeric(free_sugars_g), n)
    free_sugars_g[is.na(free_sugars_g)] <- 0
  }

  # Sodium and Salt
  if (is.null(sodium_mg)) {
    if (is.null(salt_g)) {
      sodium_mg <- rep_len(0, n)
      salt_g <- rep_len(0, n)
    } else {
      salt_g <- rep_len(as.numeric(salt_g), n)
      salt_g[is.na(salt_g)] <- 0
      sodium_mg <- salt_g * (1000 / 2.5)
    }
  } else {
    sodium_mg <- rep_len(as.numeric(sodium_mg), n)
    sodium_mg[is.na(sodium_mg)] <- 0
    if (is.null(salt_g)) {
      salt_g <- sodium_mg * 2.5 / 1000
    } else {
      salt_g <- rep_len(as.numeric(salt_g), n)
      salt_g[is.na(salt_g)] <- 0
    }
  }

  # Beneficial components
  fvns_pct <- rep_len(as.numeric(fvns_pct), n)
  fvns_pct[is.na(fvns_pct)] <- 0

  fibre_g <- rep_len(as.numeric(fibre_g), n)
  fibre_g[is.na(fibre_g)] <- 0

  protein_g <- rep_len(as.numeric(protein_g), n)
  protein_g[is.na(protein_g)] <- 0

  is_drink <- rep_len(as.logical(is_drink), n)
  is_drink[is.na(is_drink)] <- FALSE

  is_cheese <- rep_len(as.logical(is_cheese), n)
  is_cheese[is.na(is_cheese)] <- FALSE

  if (model == "2004_2005") {
    # Points Energy: 335 kJ steps
    # 0: <=335, 1: >335, 2: >670, 3: >1005, 4: >1340, 5: >1675, 6: >2010,
    # 7: >2345, 8: >2680, 9: >3015, 10: >3350
    e_breaks <- c(-Inf, 335 * (1:10), Inf)
    pts_energy <- findInterval(energy_kj, e_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_energy <- pmin(pmax(pts_energy, 0), 10)

    # Points Sat Fat: 1g steps
    # 0: <=1, 1: >1, 2: >2, ..., 10: >10
    sf_breaks <- c(-Inf, 1:10, Inf)
    pts_sat_fat <- findInterval(sat_fat_g, sf_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_sat_fat <- pmin(pmax(pts_sat_fat, 0), 10)

    # Points Total Sugars:
    # 0: <=4.5, 1: >4.5, 2: >9, 3: >13.5, 4: >18, 5: >22.5, 6: >27,
    # 7: >31, 8: >36, 9: >40, 10: >45
    sug_breaks <- c(-Inf, 4.5, 9, 13.5, 18, 22.5, 27, 31, 36, 40, 45, Inf)
    pts_sugars <- findInterval(sugars_g, sug_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_sugars <- pmin(pmax(pts_sugars, 0), 10)

    # Points Sodium (mg):
    # 0: <=90, 1: >90, ..., 10: >900
    na_breaks <- c(-Inf, 90 * (1:10), Inf)
    pts_na <- findInterval(sodium_mg, na_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_na <- pmin(pmax(pts_na, 0), 10)

    pts_a <- pts_energy + pts_sat_fat + pts_sugars + pts_na

    # Points FVN:
    # 0: <=40%, 1: >40%, 2: >60%, 5: >80%
    pts_fvns <- ifelse(fvns_pct > 80, 5,
                ifelse(fvns_pct > 60, 2,
                ifelse(fvns_pct > 40, 1, 0)))

    # Points Fibre:
    if (fibre_method == "nsp") {
      # 0: <=0.7, 1: >0.7, 2: >1.4, 3: >2.1, 4: >2.8, 5: >3.5
      fib_breaks <- c(-Inf, 0.7 * (1:5), Inf)
    } else {
      # AOAC: 0: <=0.9, 1: >0.9, 2: >1.9, 3: >2.8, 4: >3.7, 5: >4.7
      fib_breaks <- c(-Inf, 0.9, 1.9, 2.8, 3.7, 4.7, Inf)
    }
    pts_fibre <- findInterval(fibre_g, fib_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_fibre <- pmin(pmax(pts_fibre, 0), 5)

    # Points Protein: 0: <=1.6, 1: >1.6, ..., 5: >8.0
    prot_breaks <- c(-Inf, 1.6 * (1:5), Inf)
    pts_prot_raw <- findInterval(protein_g, prot_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_prot_raw <- pmin(pmax(pts_prot_raw, 0), 5)

    # Protein rule: if A < 11 OR fvns == 5 OR is_cheese == TRUE -> allowed
    prot_allowed <- (pts_a < 11) | (pts_fvns >= 5) | is_cheese
    pts_prot <- ifelse(prot_allowed, pts_prot_raw, 0)

    pts_c <- pts_fvns + pts_fibre + pts_prot
    score <- pts_a - pts_c

  } else {
    # 2018 Model
    # Points Energy: 315 kJ steps
    # 0: <=315, 1: >315, 2: >630, 3: >945, 4: >1260, 5: >1575, 6: >1890,
    # 7: >2205, 8: >2520, 9: >2835, 10: >3150
    e_breaks <- c(-Inf, 315 * (1:10), Inf)
    pts_energy <- findInterval(energy_kj, e_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_energy <- pmin(pmax(pts_energy, 0), 10)

    # Points Sat Fat:
    # 0: <=0.9, 1: >0.9, 2: >1.9, 3: >2.8, 4: >3.7, 5: >4.7, 6: >5.6,
    # 7: >6.6, 8: >7.5, 9: >8.4, 10: >9.4
    sf_breaks <- c(-Inf, 0.9, 1.9, 2.8, 3.7, 4.7, 5.6, 6.6, 7.5, 8.4, 9.4, Inf)
    pts_sat_fat <- findInterval(sat_fat_g, sf_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_sat_fat <- pmin(pmax(pts_sat_fat, 0), 10)

    # Free Sugars (use free_sugars_g if available, else sugars_g)
    sugar_use <- if (!is.null(free_sugars_g)) free_sugars_g else sugars_g
    # 0: <=0.9, 1: >0.9, 2: >1.9, 3: >2.8, 4: >3.7, 5: >4.6, 6: >5.6,
    # 7: >6.5, 8: >7.4, 9: >8.3, 10: >9.3
    sug_breaks <- c(-Inf, 0.9, 1.9, 2.8, 3.7, 4.6, 5.6, 6.5, 7.4, 8.3, 9.3, Inf)
    pts_sugars <- findInterval(sugar_use, sug_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_sugars <- pmin(pmax(pts_sugars, 0), 10)

    # Points Salt (g):
    # 0: <=0.2, 1: >0.2, 2: >0.5, 3: >0.7, 4: >0.9, 5: >1.1, 6: >1.4,
    # 7: >1.6, 8: >1.8, 9: >2.0, 10: >2.3
    salt_breaks <- c(-Inf, 0.2, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.1, 1.4, 1.6, 1.8, 2.0, 2.3, Inf)
    pts_na <- findInterval(salt_g, salt_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_na <- pmin(pmax(pts_na, 0), 10)

    pts_a <- pts_energy + pts_sat_fat + pts_sugars + pts_na

    # Points FVNS:
    pts_fvns <- ifelse(fvns_pct > 80, 5,
                ifelse(fvns_pct > 60, 2,
                ifelse(fvns_pct > 40, 1, 0)))

    # Points Fibre (AOAC up to 10 points!):
    # 0: <=0.6, 1: >0.6, 2: >1.2, ..., 10: >6.0
    fib_breaks <- c(-Inf, 0.6 * (1:10), Inf)
    pts_fibre <- findInterval(fibre_g, fib_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_fibre <- pmin(pmax(pts_fibre, 0), 10)

    # Points Protein: 0: <=1.7, 1: >1.7, 2: >3.4, 3: >5.1, 4: >6.8, 5: >8.5
    prot_breaks <- c(-Inf, 1.7 * (1:5), Inf)
    pts_prot_raw <- findInterval(protein_g, prot_breaks, left.open = TRUE) - 1
    pts_prot_raw <- pmin(pmax(pts_prot_raw, 0), 5)

    prot_allowed <- (pts_a < 11) | (pts_fvns >= 5) | is_cheese
    pts_prot <- ifelse(prot_allowed, pts_prot_raw, 0)

    pts_c <- pts_fvns + pts_fibre + pts_prot
    score <- pts_a - pts_c
  }

  # HFSS classification
  is_hfss <- ifelse(is_drink, score >= 1, score >= 4)
  healthiness <- ifelse(is_hfss, "less healthy", "healthier")

  data.frame(
    points_energy = pts_energy,
    points_sat_fat = pts_sat_fat,
    points_sugars = pts_sugars,
    points_sodium_salt = pts_na,
    points_a = pts_a,
    points_fvns = pts_fvns,
    points_fibre = pts_fibre,
    points_protein_raw = pts_prot_raw,
    protein_allowed = prot_allowed,
    points_protein = pts_prot,
    points_c = pts_c,
    npm_score = score,
    is_hfss = is_hfss,
    healthiness = healthiness,
    model = rep_len(model, n),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

#' Extract NPM Score
#'
#' Convenience wrapper around \code{\link{calculate_npm}} that returns solely
#' the final integer nutrient profile score vector.
#'
#' @param ... Arguments passed to \code{\link{calculate_npm}}.
#' @return An integer vector of nutrient profiling scores.
#' @export
npm_score <- function(...) {
  calculate_npm(...)$npm_score
}

#' Determine HFSS Status
#'
#' Convenience wrapper around \code{\link{calculate_npm}} that returns a logical
#' vector indicating whether each item is classified as High in Fat, Salt, or
#' Sugar (\code{TRUE} = less healthy / HFSS; \code{FALSE} = healthier).
#'
#' @param ... Arguments passed to \code{\link{calculate_npm}}.
#' @return A logical vector indicating HFSS status.
#' @export
is_hfss <- function(...) {
  calculate_npm(...)$is_hfss
}

#' ATNi and Vellum Scientific Plotting Themes and Palettes #' #' Consistent visual styling inspired by the Access to Nutrition Initiative (ATNi) #' public reporting language and the Vellum academic publication geometry. #' #' @name visual_styles #' @keywords internal NULL if (getRversion() >= "2.15.1") utils::globalVariables(c(".data")) # ATNi Public Style Palette atni_pal <- list( black = "#000000", white = "#FFFFFF", neutral_light = "#E4E4E4", neutral_mid = "#787878", neutral_pale = "#F2F2F2", purple = "#9658AD", blue = "#0099D9", green = "#3F783F", yellow = "#ECC441", orange = "#EE952F", red = "#B63735", pink = "#FC7984" ) # Vellum Academic Publication Theme theme_uknpm_vellum <- function(base_size = 11, base_family = "sans") { if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) { ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) + ggplot2::theme( axis.line = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "#000000", linewidth = 0.5), axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "#000000", linewidth = 0.4), axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#000000", face = "bold", size = ggplot2::rel(0.95)), axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#000000", size = ggplot2::rel(0.85)), panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "#F0F0F0", linewidth = 0.3), panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#000000", face = "bold", size = ggplot2::rel(0.9)), legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#000000", size = ggplot2::rel(0.85)), legend.background = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#F8F8F8", colour = "#000000", linewidth = 0.4), strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#000000", face = "bold", size = ggplot2::rel(0.9)) ) } } # ATNi Style Theme theme_uknpm_atni <- function(base_size = 11, base_family = "sans") { if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) { ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) + ggplot2::theme( axis.line = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "#787878", linewidth = 0.4), axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_blank(), axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#000000", face = "bold", size = ggplot2::rel(0.95)), axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#000000", size = ggplot2::rel(0.85)), panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "#E4E4E4", linewidth = 0.3), panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#000000", face = "bold", size = ggplot2::rel(0.9)), legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "#000000", size = ggplot2::rel(0.85)), legend.position = "bottom" ) } } #' Plot Healthiness Comparison Across Candidate Assessment Approaches #' #' Generates a publication-grade comparative horizontal bar chart illustrating #' the percentage of products classified as healthy versus less healthy across #' candidate UK nutritional assessment frameworks (reproducing the comparative #' reporting format of Tan et al., 2025 and ATNi product portfolio audits). #' #' @param assessment_df A data frame returned by \code{\link{assess_healthiness}} #' or \code{\link{summarise_healthiness}}. #' @param style Visual theme style: \code{"atni"} (Access to Nutrition Initiative #' editorial palette with ATNi blue and orange) or \code{"vellum"} (high-contrast #' academic publication styling). Default is \code{"atni"}. #' #' @return A \code{ggplot2} plot object. #' #' @references #' Tan M, Pham H, Pombo-Rodrigues S, et al. (2025). Nutritional composition and healthiness of out-of-home food and drink. #' \emph{Proceedings of the Nutrition Society}, 84(OCE3), E208. #' #' Access to Nutrition Initiative (2024). \emph{Global Access to Nutrition Index: Research and Scoring Methodology}. #' #' @examples #' data("sample_ooh_menu") #' assessment <- assess_healthiness(sample_ooh_menu) #' plot_healthiness_comparison(assessment, style = "atni") #' #' @export plot_healthiness_comparison <- function(assessment_df, style = c("atni", "vellum")) { if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) { stop("Package 'ggplot2' is required for plotting.") } style <- match.arg(style) # Check if input is from assess_healthiness or summarise_healthiness if (!("approach" %in% names(assessment_df))) { summary_df <- summarise_healthiness(assessment_df) } else { summary_df <- assessment_df } # Build long format for stacked horizontal bar plot approaches <- rep(summary_df$approach, 2) status <- c(rep("Healthier", nrow(summary_df)), rep("Less Healthy", nrow(summary_df))) pct <- c(summary_df$pct_healthy, summary_df$pct_less_healthy) counts <- c(summary_df$n_healthy, summary_df$n_less_healthy) labels <- sprintf("%.1f%% (%d)", pct, counts) plot_data <- data.frame( approach = factor(approaches, levels = rev(unique(summary_df$approach))), status = factor(status, levels = c("Less Healthy", "Healthier")), percentage = pct, count = counts, label = labels, stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) # Colors if (style == "atni") { fill_colors <- c("Healthier" = atni_pal$blue, "Less Healthy" = atni_pal$orange) thm <- theme_uknpm_atni() } else { fill_colors <- c("Healthier" = "#3F783F", "Less Healthy" = "#B63735") thm <- theme_uknpm_vellum() } p <- ggplot2::ggplot(plot_data, ggplot2::aes(x = .data$approach, y = .data$percentage, fill = .data$status)) + ggplot2::geom_col(position = ggplot2::position_fill(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.65, colour = "#FFFFFF", linewidth = 0.5) + ggplot2::coord_flip() + ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x * 100, "%"), expand = c(0, 0, 0.05, 0)) + ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = fill_colors, name = "Classification") + ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion of Items") + thm p } #' Plot Multiple Traffic Light (MTL) Nutrient Profile Breakdown #' #' Displays the distribution of Front-of-Pack Traffic Light ratings #' (Green / Amber / Red) across the four core nutrients (Fat, Saturated Fat, #' Total Sugars, and Salt) for an evaluated food or menu dataset. #' #' @param assessment_df A data frame returned by \code{\link{assess_healthiness}} #' or containing columns \code{mtl_fat}, \code{mtl_sat_fat}, \code{mtl_sugars}, \code{mtl_salt}. #' @param style Visual theme style: \code{"atni"} or \code{"vellum"}. #' #' @return A \code{ggplot2} plot object. #' #' @examples #' data("sample_ooh_menu") #' assessment <- assess_healthiness(sample_ooh_menu) #' plot_mtl_profile(assessment) #' #' @export plot_mtl_profile <- function(assessment_df, style = c("atni", "vellum")) { if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) { stop("Package 'ggplot2' is required for plotting.") } style <- match.arg(style) nutrients <- c("Total Fat", "Saturated Fat", "Total Sugars", "Salt") cols <- c("mtl_fat", "mtl_sat_fat", "mtl_sugars", "mtl_salt") rows_list <- list() for (k in seq_along(nutrients)) { col_name <- cols[k] if (col_name %in% names(assessment_df)) { vals <- assessment_df[[col_name]] tbl <- table(factor(vals, levels = c("Green", "Amber", "Red"))) tot <- length(vals) rows_list[[k]] <- data.frame( nutrient = nutrients[k], colour = names(tbl), count = as.numeric(tbl), pct = as.numeric(tbl) / tot * 100, stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) } } df_plot <- do.call(rbind, rows_list) df_plot$nutrient <- factor(df_plot$nutrient, levels = rev(nutrients)) df_plot$colour <- factor(df_plot$colour, levels = c("Red", "Amber", "Green")) # Official UK Traffic Light colours tl_colors <- c("Green" = "#3F783F", "Amber" = "#ECC441", "Red" = "#B63735") thm <- if (style == "atni") theme_uknpm_atni() else theme_uknpm_vellum() p <- ggplot2::ggplot(df_plot, ggplot2::aes(x = .data$nutrient, y = .data$pct, fill = .data$colour)) + ggplot2::geom_col(position = "fill", width = 0.6, colour = "#FFFFFF", linewidth = 0.5) + ggplot2::coord_flip() + ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x * 100, "%"), expand = c(0, 0, 0.05, 0)) + ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = tl_colors, name = "Traffic Light") + ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion of Items") + thm p } #' Plot NPM Score Scatter and Statutory Cutoff Boundaries #' #' Displays product distribution across Total 'A' points (negative nutrients) #' versus Total 'C' points (positive nutrients), highlighting statutory #' HFSS decision thresholds (\eqn{\text{Score} \ge 4} for food, \eqn{\ge 1} for drinks). #' #' @param data_or_assessment A data frame from \code{\link{assess_healthiness}} #' or nutritional dataset. #' @param style Visual theme style: \code{"atni"} or \code{"vellum"}. #' #' @return A \code{ggplot2} plot object. #' #' @examples #' data("sample_ooh_menu") #' assessment <- assess_healthiness(sample_ooh_menu) #' plot_npm_scatter(assessment) #' #' @export plot_npm_scatter <- function(data_or_assessment, style = c("atni", "vellum")) { if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) { stop("Package 'ggplot2' is required for plotting.") } style <- match.arg(style) df <- data_or_assessment if (!("points_a" %in% names(df))) { npm_calc <- calculate_npm( energy_kj = df$energy_kj, energy_kcal = df$energy_kcal, sat_fat_g = df$sat_fat_g, sugars_g = df$sugars_g, salt_g = df$salt_g, sodium_mg = df$sodium_mg, fvns_pct = df$fvns_pct, fibre_g = df$fibre_g, protein_g = df$protein_g, is_drink = df$is_drink ) df$points_a <- npm_calc$points_a df$points_c <- npm_calc$points_c df$npm_score <- npm_calc$npm_score df$npm_healthiness <- npm_calc$healthiness } thm <- if (style == "atni") theme_uknpm_atni() else theme_uknpm_vellum() point_colors <- if (style == "atni") { c("healthier" = atni_pal$blue, "less healthy" = atni_pal$red) } else { c("healthier" = "#3F783F", "less healthy" = "#B63735") } p <- ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(x = .data$points_c, y = .data$points_a, colour = .data$npm_healthiness)) + ggplot2::geom_abline(intercept = 4, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#787878", linewidth = 0.6) + ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) + ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = point_colors, name = "Classification") + ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 15), breaks = seq(0, 15, 3)) + ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 40), breaks = seq(0, 40, 5)) + ggplot2::labs( x = "Total 'C' Points (Beneficial: FVNS, Fibre, Protein)", y = "Total 'A' Points (Limiting: Energy, Sat Fat, Sugar, Sodium/Salt)" ) + ggplot2::annotate( "text", x = 11, y = 14, label = "Food Cutoff (A - C = 4)", angle = 32, colour = "#787878", size = 3.2, fontface = "italic" ) + thm p } #' Generate UK Nutrient Profile Model Scoring Decision Flowchart #' #' Generates the complete step-by-step decision algorithm flowchart for the UK #' Nutrient Profile Model (DHSC 2011 & 2018), displaying nutrient accumulation, #' the protein cap conditional branch, score subtraction, and the food vs drink #' statutory classification thresholds. #' #' @param format Format to generate: \code{"mermaid"} (returns Markdown Mermaid diagram string) #' or \code{"ggplot"} (draws a publication-grade flow diagram). Default is \code{"mermaid"}. #' #' @return A character string of Mermaid diagram syntax (if \code{format = "mermaid"}), #' or a \code{ggplot2} plot object (if \code{format = "ggplot"}). #' #' @export plot_npm_flowchart <- function(format = c("mermaid", "ggplot")) { format <- match.arg(format) if (format == "mermaid") { chart <- paste( "flowchart TD", " classDef inputNode fill:#F2F2F2,stroke:#787878,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#000000;", " classDef processNode fill:#EBF4FA,stroke:#0099D9,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#000000;", " classDef decisionNode fill:#FEF9E7,stroke:#EE952F,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#000000;", " classDef healthyNode fill:#EAF2EA,stroke:#3F783F,stroke-width:2px,color:#000000;", " classDef unhealthyNode fill:#FBEBEB,stroke:#B63735,stroke-width:2px,color:#000000;", "", " A1[\"Product Nutrition per 100g
(Energy, Sat Fat, Sugars, Sodium/Salt)\"]:::inputNode --> B1[\"Step 1: Calculate 'A' Points
(0-10 each, Max = 40)\"]:::processNode", " A2[\"Product Beneficial Components
(% FVNS, Fibre, Protein)\"]:::inputNode --> B2[\"Step 2: Calculate 'C' Points
(FVNS: 0-5, Fibre: 0-5, Protein: 0-5)\"]:::processNode", "", " B1 --> D1{\"Are 'A' Points ≥ 11?\"}:::decisionNode", " D1 -- \"No ('A' < 11)\" --> C1[\"Protein Points Allowed
C = FVNS + Fibre + Protein\"]:::processNode", " D1 -- \"Yes ('A' ≥ 11)\" --> D2{\"FVNS Points = 5
(or Cheese Exception)?\"}:::decisionNode", "", " D2 -- \"Yes (FVNS > 80%)\" --> C1", " D2 -- \"No (FVNS ≤ 80%)\" --> C2[\"Protein Points Capped to 0
C = FVNS + Fibre only\"]:::processNode", "", " B2 -.-> C1", " B2 -.-> C2", "", " C1 --> F1[\"Step 3: Calculate Final Score
